review: owner-approved security policy (Go-free security bug policy)
reason: Go accepts any number of check-in events in its 64 KiB body (~21.8k) in one statement under the 2 s deadline: 500s, possible late commits, duplicate events on retry and unbounded device_events. Rust caps a check-in at 100 events (real clients send 0; Go tests at most 1) and answers 400 before the proof, nonce claim or any effect.

review: owner-approved security policy (Go-free security bug policy)
reason: Go's lazy re-seal UPDATE ran without a user GUC and matched no row under devices_self, so the plaintext HMAC secret outlived every proof. Rust re-seals through rust_device_secret_reseal. It runs before HMAC verification (Go's migration position) and is idempotent: keyed on id, the exact plaintext and a NULL envelope.
